customManagers.description: biome.json carries the config schema version inside its $schema URL, and no manager reads that file — so a @biomejs/biome bump in package.json leaves the URL behind (it sat at 2.5.4 while the package was already 2.5.5, which silently validates the config against the wrong schema in the editor). This extracts the version from the URL as the same dep the npm manager already sees, so both updates share a branch and land in one PR. depTypeTemplate is what puts it under the devDependencies automerge rule below: without a depType it matches nothing, and an un-automergeable update sitting in the branch would block the automerge of the biome PR itself.

Re-reads engines.vscode as a dep whose versions come from npm @types/vscode rather than github-tags on microsoft/vscode (the npm manager's own copy is disabled in packageRules). The floor and the types then move on the same version list, so Renovate cannot propose a floor whose types are unpublished. currentValue captures only the number and leaves the ^ outside the match, so the range prefix survives the rewrite untouched. depName is deliberately not @types/vscode: that name is disabled as a devDependency, and matchPackageNames would catch this one too — packageNameTemplate carries the lookup, depNameTemplate keeps the two matchable apart.

packageRules.description: One dependency per PR. Renovate groups by default via config:recommended (all @types together, all non-major devDependencies together), which makes a single PR carry several unrelated upgrades: a red CI then names the group rather than the package that broke it, and reverting takes the innocent ones with it. `null` cancels an inherited groupName, so this rule has to sit first and every deliberate grouping below has to re-declare its own.

Majors wait for an explicit tick on the Dependency Dashboard instead of opening a PR on their own. A major is the one update that can need a code change to land, so it should arrive when someone is ready to look at it, not sit open going stale. The Renovate workflow reads this same Pending Approval section and notifies Telegram, which is what stops the list being one nobody reads.
Automerge non-major devDependency updates once CI is green — one PR each.

@types/vscode must stay in sync with engines.vscode (the minimum supported VS Code version). Never bump it automatically — raise engines.vscode by hand first. This has to be matchDepNames, not matchPackageNames: the engines floor below is resolved from packageName @types/vscode so that it can only ever target a version whose types exist, and since Renovate 39 matchPackageNames looks at packageName — `"matchPackageNames": ["@types/vscode"]` would therefore also match the floor and disable it, silently reverting this repo to never seeing an engines PR at all. depName keeps the two apart: the devDependency is @types/vscode, the floor is vscode-engines-floor.

The npm manager resolves engines.vscode from github-tags on microsoft/vscode, which is the wrong source for a floor. It offers every VS Code tag the moment it exists, including minors whose @types/vscode has not been published — #13 asked for ^1.126.0 while npm still had no @types/vscode above 1.125.0, so there was no way to raise the two together and the PR could only be closed. The floor is re-derived from npm below instead; this turns the github-tags copy off so the two do not race to open the same PR.

engines.vscode is a floor: it declares the oldest VS Code that may install the extension, and it is only honest up to the API level actually compiled against — which is @types/vscode, not whatever microsoft/vscode has tagged. So the floor is resolved from the npm versions of @types/vscode (see the customManager above), which makes an unsatisfiable bump structurally impossible: a version is only ever offered once its types are on npm to be raised alongside it. That also subsumes the old hotfix problem — #38 and #3 both landed ^1.129.1, excluding anyone on 1.129.0 for a patch that by VS Code's release model carries no new API — because @types/vscode is published sparsely and mostly on minors; allowedVersions keeps only x.y.0 in play so a stray 1.106.1 cannot become the floor. The floor may follow VS Code, but late and never by itself: minimumReleaseAge holds a fresh release back a month, automerge is off, and needs-review marks it as a human call. The reviewer still raises the @types/vscode devDependency by hand in the same PR (that one is enabled: false) — the difference is that now the version they need is guaranteed to exist.
@types/node describes the Node runtime VS Code embeds, not the one we develop on. A major bump can start type-checking against APIs the host does not ship, so it is reviewed by hand.

The one grouping that survives, and not for convenience: the runtime and the grammar are ABI-coupled, and dist/*.wasm is copied from both packages by esbuild.mjs. A PR that moves one without the other ships a runtime that cannot load the grammar it was built against, so splitting them would produce a broken PR by construction. Reviewed by hand, never automerged.

The extension host loads dist/*.wasm copied from these packages by esbuild.mjs, so a bundler bump is a packaging change. CI packages a VSIX, which is the check that matters. `minor` is listed because esbuild is still 0.x: semver calls 0.25→0.28 a minor, so a major-only rule would never fire for it and every breaking bundler release would automerge as a devDependency.
Keep GitHub Actions current and automerge them, one Action per PR. Digests are pinned by config:best-practices, so a bump is a reviewed SHA move.
